items.title: Reuters World News Summary | International
items.excerpt: Following is a summary of current world news briefs. Milan luxury shops close for fear of new unrest as government prepares to deploy troops Italy's government will dispatch 500 army troops to "defend Milan" after two days of unrest that saw demonstrators clash with police, loot shops and vandalise property, Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini said on Monday. The deployment is expected to be included in a package of security measures to be approved at a cabinet meeting ​expected on Tuesday. France in turmoil: What might follow a weekend of riots? France saw some of the worst unrest in years at the weekend as huge protests across the country over the cost of living and underfunded public services descended into riots and looting. Limoges town hall was torched ​and more than 3,000 shops were pillaged or damaged, according to the government, as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country. Killing of former anti-graft prosecutor a grim milestone in Guatemala's ‌political violence The assassination at ​the weekend of anti-graft lawyer Juan Francisco Solorzano Foppa, who made powerful enemies by taking on Guatemala's elite, marks one of the most significant political killings in the country in recent decades, renewing concerns about the vulnerability of those who fight corruption in Central America. Family, friends and supporters held a wake for Solorzano, 43, on Monday, two days after he was shot dead by two assailants at a Guatemala City sports center. His burial is scheduled for Tuesday. Pakistan army chief Asim Munir to visit Tehran on Tuesday Pakistan's army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir is due to visit Tehran on Tuesday, according to a Pakistani official and Iranian media. Pakistan has played a key mediating role between the U.S. and Iran this year. Ukraine's Zelenskiy says US decisions on Ukraine hard to explain Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday that decisions taken by the United States on the war in Ukraine, including delays in arms shipments and restrictions on intelligence sharing, were "hard to explain." "Because it all comes down to (Russian ‌President Vladimir) Putin's refusal to end this war, and to decisions on the American side that are hard to explain between friends," Zelenskiy said in a meeting with a US congressional delegation. US Supreme Court snubs bid to revive plea deal for accused 9/11 mastermind The US Supreme Court declined on Monday to hear a bid by Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, the accused mastermind of the September 11, 2001, attacks, to revive a 2024 agreement that would have spared him the death penalty in exchange for a guilty plea — a deal scrapped by former Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin. The justices turned away appeals by Mohammed and two co-defendants who had also signed plea agreements of a lower court's ruling that upheld Austin's decision to void the deals. The US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit rejected an argument that Austin, who served under former President Joe Biden, had acted too late. Alberta votes on leaving Canada, separatist movement likely to outlast expected defeat Oil-rich Alberta was holding a nonbinding referendum on Monday on whether the western province should secede from Canada, a debate ... Columbia ⁠University graduate Mahmoud Khalil on Monday asked the US Supreme Court to overturn a ruling that opened the door for President Donald Trump's administration to re-arrest and deport the Palestinian activist. Khalil's lawyers asked the justices to take up his case after the Philadelphia-based 3rd US Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that federal immigration law barred a lower-court judge from ordering his release from US Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody. Houthi attack kills 58 at Yemen government training camp, governor says Fifty-eight people were killed and more than 200 were injured after an attack on Monday by the Iran-aligned Houthis on a government security forces training camp in Yemen's Shabwa province, Governor Awad al-Wazir said, as fighting in the impoverished country intensifies. Video verified by Reuters from Shabwa province showed injured people ​and bloodied bodies scattered across the ground. Wazir also said that 14 other people remained missing after the Houthi bombardment of the Al-Alam camp. Analysis-France's unrest lays bare 'slow agony' of Macron's twilight months France’s worst bout of civil unrest in years has plunged President Emmanuel Macron’s final months in office deeper into turmoil, exposing the powerlessness of a leader struggling to contain social anger with little money to spend, scant political capital and an increasingly fragile grip on public order. The rioting that swept across France on Saturday, leaving a trail of looted shops, torched buildings and defaced public institutions, presents Macron ⁠with perhaps the most explosive challenge of his twilight presidency: a country demanding more from a state that can no longer afford to give much. Exclusive-Trump approval falls to record low of 31% as midterms near, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds President Donald Trump's approval rating fell to a record low as Americans worried about high gasoline prices and appeared ready to punish his Republican Party in the November 3 congressional elections, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that closed on Monday. Some 31% of Americans approve of Trump's performance in office, down a percentage point from two weeks earlier and the lowest level in either of his presidential terms, the four-day poll showed. Paul Mackenzie, the Kenyan preacher who led hundreds to starve to death More than three years after Kenyan police unearthed mass graves linked to a starvation cult led by evangelist Paul Mackenzie, the preacher was convicted of murder ⁠for ​the deaths of 190 children and one adult. Mackenzie's case has gripped the East African nation since officers found human remains in a forest near the Indian Ocean town of Malindi in April 2023, kicking off an investigation that would eventually unearth over 400 bodies, nearly half of them children. Brazil's government says $4 billion budget reshuffle needed for Lula measures in 2027 Brazil's Planning Ministry said on Monday that the budget reallocations needed to accommodate measures recently announced by President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva as he seeks re-election in next Sunday's vote amount to about 20 billion reais ($3.95 billion) in the 2027 budget. In a statement, the ministry said the amount represents just over 1% of total primary expenditure subject to spending limits under Brazil's fiscal framework, adding such adjustments will be made while preserving both the overall spending cap and the government's primary budget target. items.title: Hassett Says CPI Data Shows Inflation Needs ‘Some Work’
items.excerpt: Enda Curran Mon, October 19, 2026 at 9:04 AM CDT 2 min read ... (Bloomberg) -- White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said prices have been falling for items such as beef and eggs, though consumer price data for September shows overall inflation continues to need policy attention. "If you look at the previous three months, it looked like inflation was completely under control, and now it looks like it's sort of back needing some work," Hassett told CNBC Monday. Data last week showed consumer prices advanced in September at the fastest pace in five months and a gauge of underlying price pressures rose by more than expected. The consumer price index rose 0.6% from a month earlier while a key measure of underlying price pressures, which excludes food and energy, was up 0.3%. "This is either a sort of break from the downtrend or a blip," Hassett said in the interview. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh last week did nothing to dispel market expectations that the central bank will hold interest rates steady when it meets at the end of the month. In a moderated discussion at the International Monetary Fund's annual meetings, Warsh made no remarks on monetary policy or his outlook for the US economy, apart from reiterating that the Fed will deliver price stability. Hassett said he respects the central bank's independence and said Warsh will "do what he thinks is the right thing." ... "People are really euphoric about how well the economy is doing, and they're spending more. And of course, that's the kind of thing the Fed needs to pay attention to," Hassett said.

items.title: United States: October inflation seen cooling – TD Securities
items.excerpt: TD Securities economists Oscar Munoz and Eli Nir project that US headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) will rise 0.30% month-on-month in October 2026, slowing from September’s 0.65% gain, with gasoline and food still contributing. They expect core CPI to increase 0.21% and translate into a 0.24% rise in core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index, as core goods and services inflation moderate and shelter cools. ## TD sees softer but still solid CPI ... "Following the release of the September CPI report, we are providing an early look into our October projection based on multiple assumptions which may evolve as the month progresses and more data becomes available — particularly for volatile segments like gasoline prices, hotel rates, and airfares." ... "Headline inflation is expected to cool down in October, rising a still solid 0.30% m/m after a stronger 0.65% m/m September increase (CPI NSA index: 337.316 vs the market's current fixing at 337.250)." "Our preliminary forecast for the October core CPI stands at 0.21% m/m (down from a firmer 0.33% gain in September), which would be consistent with a core PCE increase at 0.24%." "Core goods prices likely lost some momentum on the back of a decline in used vehicle prices and cooling from apparel, recreation and IT goods. A pickup in household goods prices likely acted as a partial offset to the broad decline." "Services inflation is projected to mean-revert following last month's broad-based increase. We look for shelter to throttle down — led by a reversal in OER — after an unexpected surge in the last report. Slowing inflation in transportation and recreation services is also expected to help tame price gains in the segment."

items.title: US midterms: Iran war and cost of living put Trump's foreign ...
items.excerpt: October 20, 2026 - US foreign policy, particularly the Iran war, is playing an unusually prominent role in the 2026 midterm elections. - Petrol prices have risen nearly 50 per cent and diesel by two thirds since the war against Iran began in February. - Democrats have an 85 per cent chance of winning the House, though flipping the Senate remains a significantly harder task. - A Reuters/Ipsos poll found Mr Trump's approval rating at a record low of 31 per cent, driven largely by economic discontent. US foreign policy is playing an outsized role in this year's midterm elections, thanks largely to President Donald Trump's war against Iran and its effect on the cost of living for Americans. Republicans control both chambers of Congress, and Democrats are trying to win back some power on November 3, having spent two years in the political wilderness after a disastrous performance during the 2024 presidential election. A Democratic victory in either chamber would give the opposition greater powers to oppose Mr Trump's agenda, and the ability to launch investigations and call witnesses to testify about action the administration has taken. Recent polling gives the Democrats a more-than 85 per cent chance of winning the House, where they only need to flip a handful of seats. The Senate is a trickier task for Democrats, who need to gain four seats to secure a majority, including at least two in states Mr Trump carried by double digits in 2024. ... Front and centre of many political debates in the US is the cost of living, particularly petrol prices, which have risen by nearly 50 per cent since Mr Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu launched their war against Iran on February 28. Diesel, the lifeblood of the trucking industry, has been even harder hit, having risen by about two thirds. Costs for farmers, truckers and businesses have soared, with high prices being passed on to consumers in many instances. ... Polls this month show Mr Trump's approval ratings hitting new lows, with Americans particularly unhappy about the economy and cost of living. An AP-Norc survey shows that 65 per cent of US adults say higher-than-usual prices are the result of Mr Trump’s policies. This is compared to October 2022, under predecessor Joe Biden, when 44 per cent of the public said higher prices were due to presidential policies. And a Reuters/Ipsos poll published on Monday found Mr Trump's approval rating at a record low of 31 per cent. ... A Democratic majority in either or both chambers would probably increase friction with the White House over the Iran conflict, which Mr Trump has said will end one way or another immediately after the midterms. ... If they win, the Democrats are expected to hold a host of hearings, including on the true financial cost of the war and whether the US military was prepared for a new war in the Middle East. Democrats will use those hearings to try to seize an early narrative as voters start looking towards the 2028 presidential election.

items.excerpt: Quick News: Miracle, Slow, Burnout, Sicario, Posters - Dark Horizons # Quick News: Miracle, Slow, Burnout, Sicario, Posters By Garth Franklin Monday, October 19th 2026 5:14 pm DC Studios **Mister Miracle** James Gunn has released a new still from the upcoming “Mister Miracle” animated series from DC Studios. The shot is to congratulate Josh Hutcherson and Mackenzie Davis on being announced as the voice leads in the series last week – Hutcherson in the title role and Davis as Big Barda. Tom King is writing all eight episodes of the series about Scott Free, the world’s greatest escape artist and adopted son of Darkseid. [Source: X] **Slow Horses** Varada Sethu (“Doctor Who”), Tuppence Middleton (“Sense8”), Ethan Moorhouse (“Mobland”), Merab Ninidze (“Homeland”) and Joshua McGuire(“The Gold”) have all joined the cast of the seventh season of Apple TV’s “Slow Horses”. In addition, James Callis will also return as Claude Whelan after sitting out the sixth season. Adapted from the novel “Bad Actors,” Jackson Lamb and his team hunt down a mole at the heart of the British Government. [Source: Variety] **The Burnout** “Nobody 2” and “The Beekeeper 2” director Timo Tjahjanto is set to helm the action-comedy “The Burnout” at Miramax. Tom O’Connor and Hunter Toro penned the script. The story follows a washed-up former CIA agent, now living as a carefree burnout in Ibiza, is reluctantly dragged back into action. Tjahjanto remains attached to direct the film adaptation of the video game “Sleeping Dogs”. [Source: Deadline] **Sicario 3** Joshn Brolin says it was Steven Knight’s script for the third “Sicario” that finally got everyone, including co-stars Emily Blunt and Benicio del Toro, onboard to return and get the project moving. He tells THR: “Steven Knight wrote a script that was incredible, and it was kind of undeniable. All of us reacted similarly.” Padraic McKinley (“The Weight”) directs the film which will begin filming next year. **Posters** A bunch of posters today ahead of many of these titles releasing trailers tomorrow or later this week. They include the Idris Elba astronaut survival thriller “Above the Below,” the third season of Amazon’s lavish “The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power,” the next “Jumanji” film “Jumanji: Open World,” and Jeremy Saulnier’s new feature “Slayground”. > Busy poster day – "Above the Below," "LOTR: The Rings of Power," "Jumanji: Open World," "Slayground" https://t.co/6GUNWw8Bs6 > — Garth Franklin (@darkhorizons) October 20, 2026
